Agreed to run a two-week savings sandbox with Peregrine production traces and share a cost-simulation spreadsheet.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-12 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Marcus Hale (Redwood AE), Priya Sethi (Redwood SE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood), Rajiv Menon (Peregrine CTO), Sofie Park (Lead ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Infra), Maya Chen (Product)

Auto Summary (auto-generated): Live savings sim of batching + prefix/KV cache. Baseline: Peregrine currently on single model hosted endpoints, median latency 180ms, avg tokens per request 220. Redwood demo shows 25-55% unit cost reduction under realistic hit-rates. Next steps: share spreadsheet and run sandbox with traces.

Topics: batching, prefetch/prefix cache, KV cache hit-rate assumptions, concurrency/QPS, private vs hosted cost deltas, security/KMS and data retention.

[00:00] Marcus: alright thanks everyone for joining, really appreciate it. we wanted to run through a live savings scenario with some of your production-ish numbers, is that still the right ask?
[00:15] Rajiv: yep that works, thanks Marcus. we want to understand, like, is prefetching worth it for our chat flows and what happens when we go to 50 concurrent sessions.
[00:30] Priya: cool, quick note, i'll be the one toggling the sim parameters. i'll start with your baseline that Sofie sent over — avg prompt tokens ~120, avg gen tokens ~180, QPS ~6, median latency ~180ms, is that still correct?
[00:45] Sofie: yeah those look right, although the prompt tokens vary a lot on long sessions. we see some seq len spikes to 1k tokens for multi-hop contexts.
[01:00] Marcus: ok noted. i'm going to run two sims in parallel: (1) hosted path with Redwood's managed runtime and (2) private deploy on their dedicated pool assumptions — same model but quantized variant for private.
[01:20] Tom: quick infrastructure note — in private we'd need SAML + KMS integration and we prefer customer-managed KMS. is that supported?
[01:28] Priya: yes, private supports customer KMS/HSM and SAML SSO, we also emit audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 docs as part of the follow-up.
[01:40] [crosstalk] Marcus: okay starting baseline run.
[02:00] [02:00] Priya: baseline numbers loaded: 6 QPS, concurrency target 40, avg tokens 300 total. cost model used: GPU cost normalized, and hosted per-token multiplier for managed infra. showing baseline unit cost = $0.00028 per token-equivalent (internal sim unit).
[02:20] Rajiv: sorry can you repeat that unit? 0.00028?
[02:24] Priya: yep baseline effective unit, again this is a normalized number in the sim — we'll convert to your contract numbers after.
[02:35] [02:35] Priya: now enabling batching with continuous batching window at 15ms and max batch size 32, and enabling prefix cache (we'll simulate K V cache hit-rate at 18%).
[02:50] Marcus: note — prefix cache covers repeated system or shared context, kv cache is session-specific retrievals, for us we model both.
[03:05] Sofie: ok show me what that does to latency tail. our tail matters more than median.
[03:15] Priya: agree. sim shows median latency increases by ~10ms due to batching aggregation but p95 improves because of cache hits reducing work — p95 went from 420ms down to 320ms in this sim at 18% hit-rate.
[03:40] Tom: that seems counterintuitive, median up but p95 down?
[03:45] Priya: yeah because small micro-batching adds a sliver of wait for many requests but cache hits turn expensive generation into cheap lookup for a subset, which shaves off heavy tail cases.
[04:00] [04:00] Rajiv: what's the throughput improvement?
[04:05] Priya: effective tokens per second per GPU improved by ~1.6x in the sim given your request mix. that translates to lower required GPU-hours for the same QPS.
[04:20] Marcus: on cost side the sim reports a 38% reduction in per-session token cost at 18% hit-rate with batching enabled. going to show a sensitivity sweep now.
[04:35] [04:35] Priya: sweep running — x-axis is cache hit-rate from 0% to 60%, y-axis is percent savings versus baseline. at 0% hit-rate batching alone gives ~12% savings, at 30% hit-rate we hit ~52% savings.
[04:55] Sofie: 52% is big — what assumptions about cache warmup are you making?
[05:00] Priya: good question. warmup modeled from a 48h trace you provided but anonymized; we assume cold start on new sessions and warm prefixes for returning users, warmup period ~6 hours for most common patterns.
[05:20] Maya: can you explain how you count tokens for cached hits? do we still pay generation tokens?
[05:28] Marcus: cached hits bypass decoder GPU work so effective generation tokens are near-zero for those requests, we still bill a tiny retrieval cost (index lookup/IO) — modeled as ~0.2% of generation cost.
[05:40] Tom: and for private deploy, if we use lower-precision quantization, what does that change?
[05:50] Priya: quantized runtime reduces GPU memory and kernel execution time — in the sim private quantized variant cuts per-token execution cost by another ~18% compared to hosted high-precision kernels, but costs for ops like KV lookup and network transfer remain.
[06:10] [06:10] Rajiv: any model-quality risk with that quantized variant? we can't degrade chat quality noticeably.
[06:18] Priya: we tag quantization profiles per-model and run small regen tests — for your Llama-derived model the 4-bit profile preserved quality in our evals across your prompt suite. we'll include the regen comparisons in the spreadsheet.
[06:35] Sofie: show me a scenario where batching hurts us. i want to understand worst-case latency for interactive flows.
[06:45] Priya: toggling to strict latency SLO mode: setting max batching window to 3ms and prefer route to low-latency pool — savings drop to ~8% but p95 falls below 250ms. so there's a clear tradeoff knob.
[07:05] Marcus: also note session-affinity matters — if you can route repeated sessions to the same model worker, KV cache locality improves hit-rate.
[07:20] [07:20] Priya: now running a multitenant stress sim — we mimic bursty QPS up to 24 and concurrency 80. cache hit-rate drops to 10% in that pattern, savings fall accordingly to ~22%.
[07:40] Rajiv: so for our holiday traffic spikes, prefetch might be less effective?
[07:45] Priya: prefetch can be scheduled for known peak patterns: we can pre-warm common prefixes during off-peak windows and keep a LRU of heavy prefixes. that recovers some hit-rate during peaks.
[08:05] Sofie: what about memory/infra overhead of prefix caches, we have limited host memory in private cluster.
[08:15] Priya: prefix cache uses compact serialized KV entries; in the sim we modeled 150MB total for your top-100k prefix entries — that's configurable. memory overhead scales with number of cached keys and average prefix length.
[08:35] Tom: do we get metrics on hit-rate and cache churn? we need visibility.
[08:42] Marcus: yes Console exposes token-level breakdown by route and cache hit metrics per model and per route. we'll show those dashboards in the next deep-dive.
[09:00] [09:00] Maya: questions on security — where is the cache stored in hosted? what if prefixes contain PII?
[09:10] Priya: hosted stores prefix cache encrypted at rest in our managed KMS with tenant separation, and you can opt-out of caching specific routes; for private you control the storage and can enforce stricter retention.
[09:30] Rajiv: retention policies? we need 30-day auditability for some customers.
[09:36] Marcus: Console allows retention configuration and audit logs export to your SIEM; we also support longer retention as beta add-on.
[09:50] [09:50] Priya: switching to cost breakout, i'll open the spreadsheet. baseline monthly cost estimate with your current QPS is $42k for hosted. with batching + prefix @ 18% hit we show $26k. with private + quantized variant we show $21k (includes reserved capacity assumptions).
[10:10] Sofie: those are big numbers, how confident are you in the 21k private figure?
[10:15] Priya: +/- 12% uncertainty depending on real hit-rate and sequence length distribution — we'll reduce that after we run your trace in the sandbox.
[10:30] [10:30] Marcus: i'll annotate the spreadsheet with the key sensitivity levers — seq len, hit-rate, concurrency.
[10:42] Rajiv: how would rollouts look? can we A/B test caching policies?
[10:50] Priya: yes Console supports rollout flags per route — you can canary cache-enabled routes to a subset of users and monitor quality regressions via evals.
[11:05] Tom: on-network for private, what do we need to open? egress?
[11:10] Priya: private deploys can be in VPC with no public egress if desired; if you want Redwood-managed control-plane we need port 443 to our control plane IPs for orchestration; or we can do fully air-gapped with an on-prem package.
[11:30] Marcus: ok i'm toggling to show a scenario with higher prefix reuse — set hit-rate to 42%. this is more like a support-bot where many users share context.
[11:45] [11:45] Priya: results: at 42% hit-rate and batch size 24 we get 57% savings vs baseline and p95 at 210ms. required GPUs reduce from 6 to 2 for your target QPS in the sim.
[12:05] Sofie: if that's true we should prioritize prefix generation in our ingestion pipeline. how do we build those prefixes?
[12:12] Marcus: there are two patterns — (1) deterministic prefix templates for product flows, (2) learned clustering of recent conversation turns. Redwood Optimize can suggest top-k prefixes based on your traces. we'll include suggested prefix lists in the follow-up.
[12:30] [12:30] Rajiv: do you support TTL per-key? we want to expire sensitive prefixes quickly.
[12:36] Priya: yes TTL and route-level TTLs, also encryption-in-use for private if you want HSM-bound keys.
[12:50] Maya: what's the billing model for dedicated reserved capacity? is there a commit?
[12:58] Marcus: Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual capacity. we modeled reserved discount in the spreadsheet; private on prem is license + support. we'll include pricing scenarios side-by-side.
[13:15] [13:15] Tom: any pitfalls we've missed? corners where this breaks?
[13:20] Priya: corner cases: very high entropy prompts (unique completions) yield low cacheability; also extremely bursty unpredictable traffic reduces batching efficiency. we flag these in the sim and show fallback policies.
[13:40] Rajiv: okay what do you need from us to run the sandbox?
[13:45] Marcus: 48 hour anonymized traces, target SLOs (p50/p95), a list of routes you want to evaluate and a decision on hosted vs private for the pilot.
[13:58] Sofie: we can provide traces and we'll try to set expectations with product.
[14:10] [14:10] Priya: final slide — recommended pilot: 2-week sandbox, Redwood runs cost sim + caching suggestions, we instrument Console dashboards and share regen quality checks. goal: quantify real savings and safety checks.
[14:30] Maya: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[14:35] Rajiv: quick note, please include the kernel selection notes; our infra person wants to know what kernels are used for quantized runs.
[14:44] Priya: will attach kernel mapping table and perf profiles.
[14:50] Marcus: okay we'll follow up with the spreadsheet and SOC2 + examples. thanks all.
[14:58] [End of meeting]
